function: Multi-agent DRL jointly selects UAV uplink channels (spectrum allocation), trajectories, and user associations in multi-UAV MEC under jamming, minimizing delay and maximizing semantic accuracy (pp. 4, 7, 8).
system: 2 UAVs at 100 m receive from 2 vehicles and 5 RSUs over orthogonal channels; scalar (single-antenna) links, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 4-6, 11).
method: Multi-agent twin delayed DDPG (SC-MA-TD3), one agent per UAV, fully connected actor and critic networks (128, 64 neurons); online reinforcement learning; pre-trained DeepSC-VQA codec used as given (pp. 8-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: elevation-dependent LoS/NLoS probability path loss with free-space loss and Rayleigh CN(0,1) fading for user and jammer links; same for training and testing (pp. 5-6).
test_conditions: Online training and evaluation in one simulated area (2 UAVs, 12 image points, 5 RSUs, moving jammer); sweeps of jamming power 14-22 dBm, semantic symbols k, modality (pp. 10-13).
baselines: Learned: SC-D4N (DDPG of [24] plus DDQN of [43]), SC-MA-DDPG (MA-DDPG [35]); non-learned: SC-MA-TD3-F with fixed actions; variants: N-SC-MA-TD3 (no semantic communication), reward-weight variants (pp. 11, 14).
metrics: Accumulated reward, communication and computation delay per episode, semantic accuracy per episode, and semantic rate in suts/s (pp. 11-14).
complexity: Training complexity O(NET(2∑(U_{u-1}U_u+U_uU_{u+1})+4∑(V_{v-1}V_v+V_vV_{v+1}))) for N agents, E epochs, T slots, actor and critic layer sizes (p. 11); no runtime.
q1_support: p. 5: "we address a widely used path loss model that includes both LoS and NLoS links"; p. 6: "is the Rayleigh fading coefficient". Custom simulator (LoS-probability path loss plus Rayleigh fading); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 9: "The DRL algorithm used in this paper is an online DRL algorithm that interacts with a dynamic environment"; p. 12: results "under varying jamming power levels". Only sweeps of jamming power, semantic symbols, and modality; no trained model is tested in a scenario unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 11: "SC-D4N approach: Combining Semantic Communication technology with the DDPG algorithm presented in [24] and the double deep Q-network (DDQN) algorithm presented in [43]"; "SC-MA-TD3-F approach: all actions being fixed values"; p. 12: "compares the accumulated communication and computation delay and semantic accuracy per episode among different approaches".
q4_support: p. 11: "the total computational complexity of the MATD3 algorithm during training is O(NET(2∑(Uu−1Uu + UuUu+1) + 4∑(Vv−1Vv + VvVv+1)))".
q5_support: p. 11: "all moving or remaining stationary within a 1000 × 1000m area" (synthetic simulation); p. 5: semantic data "similar to those in [38], [39]". No code or data link and no public channel dataset.
notes: Include as area 6, with a borderline eligibility call for the reviewer. The learned MA-TD3 decides UAV trajectories and user associations (above PHY) jointly with channel selection, which the paper frames as spectrum allocation on the UAV uplink, p. 4: "the channels for each UAV to receive image tasks need to be selected to allocate spectrum resources reasonably" (N image channels "with unequal bandwidth sizes"). By the aerial-link rule, learned resource allocation is physical layer, so the joint decision passes above_phy and fits area 6 (resource control for aerial links); single-antenna links are admitted for NTN. Caveat: jamming is the scenario (index term "anti-jamming"; p. 8: channel selections adjusted "to counteract the jamming"), so the reviewer may instead read the function as anti-jamming and exclude with code function; the stated objective is delay and semantic accuracy, not anti-jamming alone (p. 7). The semantic codec DeepSC-VQA is pre-trained and not learned in this work (p. 5). q1: the LoS-probability path loss model cited from [17], [41] is not a standardized channel model. q3: the non-learned baseline is the fixed-action SC-MA-TD3-F (no learned decisions); learned baselines SC-D4N and SC-MA-DDPG are compared on delay and semantic accuracy (Figs. 5-7, pp. 12-13). Figure axes and the complexity formula were read from the PDF images of pp. 10-14. Title and DOI on p. 1 match the record.
